verify.heading: Verify library
verify.intro: Checks that every original file is still there and unchanged. Verifying only reports what it finds: nothing is changed or deleted, and it works in a read-only library.
verify.startFailed: The check could not be started: {{message}}
verify.cancelled: The check was cancelled; nothing was recorded.
verify.originalsFine: Every original is there and unchanged.
verify.clean: Nothing was found: every original is there and unchanged.
verify.thumbnails_one: {{count}} thumbnail is missing; it is made again when it is needed.
verify.thumbnails_other: {{count}} thumbnails are missing; they are made again when they are needed.
verify.strayHeading: Folders that belong to no roll or frame (never deleted)

keys.heading: Keyboard
keys.intro: The keys for the Develop view. Change one by choosing Change and pressing the new key; Escape cancels. A key can belong to one action only. A change is saved at once and applies the next time the Develop view opens.
keys.colourNote: A press moves a colour slider by 10 steps, Shift and the key by 1. Shift never changes which action a key means.
keys.press: Press the new key for “{{action}}”. Escape cancels.
keys.taken: {{key}} is already used for “{{action}}”. Choose another key, or change that one first.
keys.invalid: {{key}} cannot be a shortcut. Use a letter, a digit or a punctuation mark.
keys.modified: Press the key on its own, without Ctrl, Alt or Command.

develop.backToLibrary: Back to the Library (first stops picking)

look.heading: Starting look
look.intro: What the automatic conversion of frames you import from now on starts from. Frames already imported keep their recipes; in Develop, Curves has a button to apply the look to one frame.
look.label: Starting look
look.film_log: Film log (Blackmagic Film Gen 5): a flat, wide-latitude start for editing
look.frontier: Frontier style: a contrasty, saturated lab-print look, fitted to Trichroma Lab
look.saveFailed: The starting look could not be saved: {{message}}

flags.heading: Feature flags
flags.intro: Switches for features that can be turned off if they misbehave. A change is saved at once. A flag takes effect where its feature is used, as that feature arrives.

dust_removal.name: Infrared dust removal
dust_removal.purpose: Turn it off if the infrared cleaning misbehaves on real scans.

triplet_import.name: RGB triplet import
triplet_import.purpose: Allows importing separate red, green and blue exposures. Turn it off until it is verified.

guided_capture.name: Guided capture
guided_capture.purpose: Scanlight control and camera capture. Turn it off if the hardware misbehaves.

dev_overlay.name: Developer overlay
dev_overlay.purpose: Shows per-stage timings and memory in the Develop view.

experimental_auto_levels.name: Experimental auto levels
experimental_auto_levels.purpose: An alternative way to find the black and white points.

update_check.name: Check for updates
update_check.purpose: Asks GitHub Releases for a newer version when the app starts, at most once a day. Turn it off to make no network request at all.

updates.heading: Updates
updates.intro: Grain to Pixel asks GitHub Releases whether a newer version exists. It sends nothing about you or your library, and it never installs anything without your say.
updates.off: The update check is switched off. Switch on “Check for updates” in the feature flags below to use this button.

about.heading: About and licences
about.rawler: Grain to Pixel uses rawler to read camera NEF files, under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1. You can rebuild the app with a modified rawler: see docs/rebuild-with-rawler.md in the source.
about.licence: The licence of Grain to Pixel
about.components: The licence text of every component
about.componentsFailed: The licence texts could not be loaded: {{message}}

diagnostics.heading: Diagnostics
diagnostics.intro: If something goes wrong, you can save a zip with the logs, the versions, your feature flags, the counters below and the last job errors. It holds no pictures and no folder names, and nothing is sent anywhere: you decide whether to share it.
diagnostics.countersNote: These stay in your library and are used only to see how far the app got.
diagnostics.noLibrary: Open a library to see its counters.

update.installing: Downloading the update and checking its signature…
update.installed: The update is installed. Restart to use it.

apply.title: Apply settings
apply.description: Copy groups of settings from one frame to others. This replaces those settings on the other frames.

hint.Color: Balance, temperature, tint, saturation and black and white.
hint.Tone: Exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, dehaze and the curves.
hint.Geometry: The crop, turns, flips and straightening. Frames are not always cropped the same.
hint.Base: Where the film base comes from, and its values.
hint.Invert: The black and white points of the inversion.
hint.Output: The amount and radius of the sharpening applied when exporting.

apply.confirm_one: This replaces the {{groups}} settings on {{count}} frame, whatever they were. It cannot be undone.
apply.confirm_other: This replaces the {{groups}} settings on {{count}} frames, whatever they were. It cannot be undone.
apply.noGroups: Choose at least one group of settings.

crop.useAsRollFrame: Use this crop as the roll’s frame size

crop.rollFrameFailed: The roll’s frame size could not be set: {{message}}

ratio.label: Aspect ratio
ratio.invalid: Use positive numbers; the ratio can be at most 20 to 1 either way.
ratio.locked: The crop keeps the ratio {{ratio}} (width to height) as the finished picture.

dust.heading: Dust removal
dust.note: Removes the dust and scratches that the infrared plane of the scan shows. The preview uses a smaller copy of the plane, so very fine specks may only disappear in the exported file.
dust.flagOff: Dust removal is switched off in Settings, so these controls have no effect until it is switched on.

sharpen.heading: Output sharpening
sharpen.note: Applied when you export, not in the preview, so nothing on screen changes. The radius is in pixels of the exported image: a smaller export wants a smaller radius.

curve.startingLookDone: The master curve is now the one of the Starting look in Settings.

import.title: Import
import.needsLibrary: Open or create a library in the Library view first.

scanner.heading: Scan a roll
scanner.intro: Scans frames of a roll with the Nikon Coolscan LS-50. Each frame is stored as soon as it is scanned, so stopping or an error keeps the frames before it, and you can continue from the next one.
scanner.none: No scanner was found. Check that it is on and connected.
scanner.driverHint: On Windows the scanner needs the WinUSB driver for this app (see docs/research/nkscan.md); with another scanning program's driver it is listed but cannot be used.
scanner.fresh: No frame of this roll has been scanned yet.
scanner.resume: Frames before {{n}} have been scanned. Continue at frame {{n}}.
scanner.complete: All 40 frames of this roll have been scanned.
scanner.ir: Also scan the infrared (for dust removal)
scanner.frameRange: A frame is a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.
scanner.frameOrder: The last frame must not come before the first.
scanner.previewFailed: The roll could not be previewed: {{message}}
scanner.previewAlt: The whole roll as the scanner sees it, {{count}} frames side by side
scanner.previewCaption: {{count}} frames found. The lines mark where the frames start if they are evenly spaced.

capture.heading: Capture with the camera
capture.intro: Shoots each frame as a red, green and blue exposure with the Scanlight and the camera, merges them and stores the frame in the chosen roll. The light is switched off when you leave this view.

light.tripped: Light too hot and switched off
light.warmHint: The light is getting warm. Capturing goes on, but let it cool down between rolls.
light.lowSupply: The USB supply of the light is low ({{mv}} mV). Use another port or a powered hub.

levels.needTest: Take a test shot at these levels to save them.
levels.exposureDiffers: The camera settings differ from when these levels were saved.

liveView.heading: Live view
liveView.help: Live view does not turn the light on by itself: choose a colour here.
liveView.macOnly: Live view is available on macOS only for now.
liveView.sharpnessMeter: Sharpness now, against the best since live view or the zoom started
liveView.areaHint: Click the picture to choose the spot to zoom to, or move it with the arrows.
liveView.pickArea: Choose the spot to zoom to (the middle, when pressed with the keyboard)

test.clippedUnknown: How much is clipped is not known.
test.clipWarning: The {{channel}} test shot is clipped ({{pct}} %). Lower its level.

focusCheck.heading: Focus check
focusCheck.label: Focus check
focusCheck.help: Takes one picture in the chosen colour and shows the middle of it at full size, with a sharpness number and a map of how sharp each part of the frame is. Nothing is stored.
focusCheck.cropAlt: The middle of the {{channel}} picture at full size
focusCheck.map: Sharpness of each part of the frame, the sharpest part is 100 %
focusCheck.mapAgainst: Sharpness of each part of the frame against the flat reference, the best part is 100 %

pattern.flat: The film looks flat and square to the camera.
pattern.bowed: The middle is sharper than the edges: the film is bowed or the holder sags.
pattern.tilted: The {{side}} is softer: the film or the holder is tilted.

focusCheck.caveat: Fair only on even texture (grain in an evenly exposed area, or a flat target such as a printed fine pattern). A wide aperture (f/4 to f/5.6) shows the differences best.

calibrate.label: Calibrate
calibrate.help: Frame clear film base, such as the leader, with nothing else lit: no bare light past the film's edge. The black carrier and mask are fine.
calibrate.coarse: {{channel}} ended at level {{level}}, where one step is a big change, so it can't be set finely. This is normal when one colour of the light is much stronger than the others.

next.label: Next frame (Space)

next.thumbnail: The frame that was just captured

files.intro: Choose the NEF files of a roll shot as red, green and blue exposures. They are grouped by capture time into triplets; check the order of each one, confirm the ones to import, and start.
